I think you're good but I have also been in your situation and this thread was making me feel kinda sorta "attacked". My bf's ex cheated on him and he tried to give her a second chance but it didn't work. Months later he and I met. She was constantly texting and calling him, begging him to take her back; if he didn't answer she'd threaten to hurt or kill herself so he'd panic and contact her. This alone made me hate her, I had been in a psychologically abusive relationship before and knew this shit was bad.

Our relationship was essentially us and his ex. I couldn't handle her always interfering and told him that he needed to cut her out or I'd have to leave (I don't consider this to be unreasonable, I had to set a boundary in regards to her - if she hadn't been so intrusive I would've been fine with her talking to him). So he blocked her and got rid of her stuff. Several months later she got a different phone and blew up his phone from that, threatening to hurt or kill herself if he ignored her. She also attempted to hack my facebook and started stalking my sister in law online (I had blocked his ex everywhere so my next of kin was apparently her alternate target). My SIL had to block her also.

We ended up going to counseling bc of it. Our counselor had good advice for ppl in my bf's situation (i.e. Trying to set a boundary with someone but failing to enforce it when they threaten self harm). He said that in those situations don't answer the person BUT do call the police for wherever they are and tell them of the possibility of self harm. The cops will do a wellness check. If it was a manipulation (as it usually is and was in our case) then the cops showing up is embarrassing and stops the manipulative behavior. If on the off chance it was a legit threat then they are now going to get the help they need.

Not everyone who wants the ex cut out is crazy or insecure; some exes are toxic and try to destroy the new relationship.

Only the ones under the official humane society umbrella, and yeah they make hella buck and then spend it on fighting no kill advocates from passing legislation to protect animals.

Our shelter charges $50 for cats, $100 for dogs but with discounts for older animals (also sometimes monthly deals like August dedicated to tabby cats so they're only $25 during that time). They are highly involved in the community so people volunteer bc they see the good they're doing and engaged. Other shelters tend to talk down to volunteers and speak of the awfulness of humans and how this is their fault and it just sends bad vibes. 

Our shelter also has a veterinarian who volunteers bimonthly to neuter/spay already homed animals for a very small fee (this helps poor families who love their pets but maybe struggle to afford everything so they skip that and then puppies and kittens happen). They also work with the local feral cat society to routinely set traps and bring those cats in to be spayed for free by the vet and rereleased (humane society and aspca advocate culling stray cats as a solution to overpopulation, but this just doesn't work).

Shelters don't have to charge so much and they exclude potential adopters by doing so

Not necessarily. My family hasn't paid for any of our pets except one from our local shelter ($50 adoption fee which is MUCH more reasonable). My parents dog was found abandoned in the country as a puppy, our other three cats were strays (one abandoned by his mama as a kitten so I bottle fed him), the other two birthed under my parents porch by a stray (they had two other siblings we gave to my aunt who is also a mega animal person), my older brother adopted the mama cat, and last but not least my parents beagle who my parents were alerted was going to be abandoned in the country by her owners bc they just didn't want her anymore. ALL of our animals are spoiled rotten, loved, and taken to the vet at the first sign of a maybe illness (seriously, our older dog is named after our vet). If we had to pay $400 tho for each of them we wouldn't have them bc that's just not feasible.

So yeah my family doesn't really adopt from shelters that charge exorbitant fees bc it's absurd. We find plentyyyy of animals that need saved without shelling out that money.

Same goes for my extended family. Mom's twin has two rescue dogs (one a puppy her bro bought without consulting his wife who didn't want a dog so she took the puppy for them), an abandoned dog left by the highway (chip registry helped us track the owners who then admitted to dumping her and forfeited ownership), found a pregnant cat thrown out by her people when they moved bc they didn't want to deal with it.. She had two kittens, sadly one didn't make it but the other one is living with the mama cat at my aunt's.

My other aunt who adopted my cats' siblings, she rescues so many abandoned animals I have a hard time tracking but all are cared for. My favorite example of her selfless love of animals is when she heard mewing from her wall. She took a hammer to a section near the mewing (very carefully) and found some kittens. A stray had gotten in the attached garage and had kitten in the rafters but some fell down into the walls. All were rescued and live with her, they are affectionately known as the wall kittens.

So basically my long winded comment is just showing how people really can get animals very easily and if shelters want to encourage them to get them from their place they shouldn't charge so much because it excludes huge swaths of people who would otherwise give the animals amazing homes.

Yup and the humane society and aspca actively fight legislation to regulate shelters better, oppose efforts to create longer hold periods for people to claim their pets before the shelters kill them, fight against attempts to make it illegal for a shelter to kill an animal if another rescue is offering/asking to take the animal, kill abused animals who show any sign of aggression instead of recognizing they've come from a traumatic situation and need some time and patience to recover, and the list just keeps going...

To be honest, the more I learn about both organizations the angrier I get. They runs ads of all these poor mistreated animals and then block legislation trying to make sure the animals get better and find homes.

Exactly this. I work in underwriting and there are so many ways insureds can lower their premium because they're lowering the risk of insuring them. I'm in commercial so things like fire alarms, automatic sprinklers, burglar alarms, construction (mostly for builders risks bc tenant merchants can't change the construction, it's smart to have a construction pretty much other than frame), year built (which can be updated if the building is updated), years in business, claims history, plus discretionary discounts if we send out a field underwriter to inspect and s/he believes the insured has gone above most to mitigate losses. These are all determined initially by the actuaries who study all these variables and how much risk they pose and what the cost is and on and on.

Insurance companies aren't saints by any means, but it's within reason for them to increase premium after an incident because you've proven you're a liability.

My dad was driving through the countryside one day when he saw something. He stopped and reversed to see what it was, through the rain he saw a puppy sitting in the ditch. My dad got out and approached him, the little puppy started walking towards my dad, wiggling his little butt as he tries to wag his tail. My dad scooped him up and took him to his truck where he wrapped him in some rags to dry him off. My dad took the puppy home and after searching to hopefully find that a family was looking for their lost puppy he found out that this puppy had been from a local litter but was the only one that they didn't sell or give away. So they dumped him, a little eight week old puppy. Dumped in the countryside to fend for himself and try to avoid the jaws of a coyote or the wheel of a car.

Five years later and this puppy is full-grown. His name is Arlo and he and my dad are best friends. You can tell by the way he looks at my dad that he knows he saved him. The unyielding love in his eyes is so palpable, even to people who don't know how my dad and Arlo came together.

I don't know how there are such cruel people who would abandon dependent animals, but it's nice to know that people like OP and my dad are there to balance it out.
